knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Approximate optimizer-selection recovery object
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V(x)=\sup_{y\in Y}\phi(x,y)\) be finite and convex on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), with no assumption that the supremum is attained. Fix \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex maximum-value functions at the boundary between exact optimizer selection and recovery from approximate selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varepsilon>0\), define the approximate optimizer set \[Y_\varepsilon(x_0):=\{y\in Y:\phi(x_0,y)\ge V(x_0)-\varepsilon\}.\] Define the nearby approximate-selection subgradient set \[G_\varepsilon(x_0):=\bigcup\{\partial_x\phi(x,y):y\in Y_\varepsilon(x_0),\ \|x-x_0\|\le\varepsilon\}.\] The approximate-selection recovery object is \[\mathcal R(x_0):=\bigcap_{\varepsilon>0}\overline{\operatorname{co}}G_\varepsilon(x_0).\] The recovery boundary separates exact selection, where an optimizer set generates \(\partial V(x_0)\) directly, from nonattainment, where the closure-intersection object is required. In the supported finite-valued convex regime, \(\partial V(x_0)=\mathcal R(x_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When exact optimizers are unavailable, one selects parameters whose values are arbitrarily close to optimal, permits their subgradients to be evaluated at nearby points, then takes closed convex hulls and intersects over vanishing tolerances. This limiting object is the approximate-selection recovery object and recovers the value-function subdifferential in the finite-dimensional finite-valued convex setting.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Recovery may be computed along any sequence \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\).
special_cases_latex: If stable exact optimizers exist, the limiting construction reduces to the active-optimizer formula.
immediate_consequences_latex: The construction remains meaningful when \(Y(x_0)=\varnothing\).
boundary_notes: Approximate optimality at \(x_0\) alone may be insufficient; nearby evaluation points are part of the recovery construction.
The record does not claim compactness of approximate optimizer sets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonattainment invalidates formulas requiring an exact minimizing selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The function \(F(x,y)=x+e^y\) is finite and convex. For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}\),
\[
p(x)=\inf_{y\in\mathbb{R}}(x+e^y)=x,
\]
yet the infimum is not attained because \(e^y>0\) for every finite \(y\). Therefore \(\partial p(x)=\{1\}\), while the union of projected joint subgradients over exact minimizers is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex marginal can have subgradients although its infimum is never attained, making exact-selection formulas empty.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonattained Infima

children.title: Approximate Optimizer Selections
children.top_down_role: Near-minimizing parameter selections used for subgradient recovery.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate minimizing selections for possibly unattained marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(p(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y)>-\infty\), define the \(\varepsilon\)-optimizer set by
\[
Y_\varepsilon(x):=\{y\in Y:F(x,y)\le p(x)+\varepsilon\}.
\]
A mapping \(y_\varepsilon\) satisfying \(y_\varepsilon(x)\in Y_\varepsilon(x)\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-optimizer selection. Exact optimizers correspond to \(\varepsilon=0\), whereas positive tolerances permit recovery when the infimum is not attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An epsilon-optimizer selection chooses a feasible point whose objective value is within epsilon of the marginal infimum.

children.title: Closure Recovery
children.top_down_role: Closure structures compensating for unavailable exact optimizers.

assumptions_latex: \(p(x)=\inf_yF(x,y)\) is proper lower-semicontinuous convex and finite at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional marginal recovery from approximate minimizers and approximate subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(\varepsilon>0\), let \(Y_\varepsilon(\bar x)=\{y:F(\bar x,y)\le p(\bar x)+\varepsilon\}\). Then
\[
\partial p(\bar x)=\bigcap_{\varepsilon>0}\overline{\{u:\exists y\in Y_\varepsilon(\bar x),\ (u,0)\in\partial_{2\varepsilon}F(\bar x,y)\}}.
\]
Thus exact marginal subgradients are recovered as closed limits of horizontal approximate joint subgradients evaluated at increasingly accurate optimizer selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing and intersecting horizontal approximate joint subgradients over increasingly accurate minimizers recovers the marginal subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.title: Closure Recovery

children.top_down_role: Subgradient compatibility organized by exact and nonattained decompositions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Infimal convolution and compatible-subgradient family
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f_1,f_2:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper convex functions with a common affine minorant.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex infimal convolution, distinguishing exact from nonattained decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The infimal convolution is \[(f_1\square f_2)(x):=\inf_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{f_1(y)+f_2(x-y)\}=\inf_{x_1+x_2=x}\{f_1(x_1)+f_2(x_2)\}.\] Its exact decomposition set and \(\varepsilon\)-decomposition set are \[D(x):=\{(x_1,x_2):x_1+x_2=x,\ f_1(x_1)+f_2(x_2)=(f_1\square f_2)(x)\},\] \[D_\varepsilon(x):=\{(x_1,x_2):x_1+x_2=x,\ f_1(x_1)+f_2(x_2)\le(f_1\square f_2)(x)+\varepsilon\}.\] For \((x_1,x_2)\in D(x)\), the compatible-subgradient set is \[C(x_1,x_2):=\partial f_1(x_1)\cap\partial f_2(x_2),\] and the exact infimal-convolution rule is \(\partial(f_1\square f_2)(x)=C(x_1,x_2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infimal convolution minimizes the sum of two functions over all decompositions of \(x\). The rule family records exact and approximate decomposition sets. At an exact decomposition, a subgradient is compatible when it belongs simultaneously to the subdifferential of the first term at the first component and that of the second term at the second component; this common set is the subdifferential of the infimal convolution.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The operation is the infimal image of \((x_1,x_2)\mapsto f_1(x_1)+f_2(x_2)\) under \((x_1,x_2)\mapsto x_1+x_2\).
special_cases_latex: If \(f_2(z)=\|z\|^2/2\), the operation is a Moreau-type regularization.
immediate_consequences_latex: At any two exact decompositions, the displayed intersection represents the same set \(\partial(f_1\square f_2)(x)\).
boundary_notes: Even for closed convex inputs, an infimal convolution need not be closed.
The exact intersection formula requires \(D(x)\neq\varnothing\).

children.title: Exact Infimal Decompositions
children.top_down_role: Subgradient structure supported by attained infimal decompositions.

assumptions_latex: \((f\square g)(\bar x)=\inf_z\{f(z)+g(\bar x-z)\}\) is finite and attained at \(\bar z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial(f\square g)(\bar x)=\partial f(\bar z)\cap\partial g(\bar x-\bar z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact infimal-convolution rule at an attained decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose
\[
(f\square g)(\bar x)=f(\bar z)+g(\bar x-\bar z).
\]
Then the subdifferential of the infimal convolution is exactly
\[
\partial(f\square g)(\bar x)=\partial f(\bar z)\cap\partial g(\bar x-\bar z).
\]
Hence a vector is a subgradient of the marginal value precisely when it is simultaneously a subgradient of both terms at the two components of the attained decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an attained infimal decomposition, the infimal-convolution subdifferential is the intersection of the component subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Infimal Decompositions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact infimal decomposition and common subgradient
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f_1,f_2:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper convex functions whose infimal convolution is proper, and fix \(x\in\operatorname{dom}(f_1\square f_2)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise attained infimal convolution in finite-dimensional convex analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pair \((\bar x_1,\bar x_2)\) is an exact infimal decomposition of \(x\) when \[\bar x_1+\bar x_2=x,\qquad (f_1\square f_2)(x)=f_1(\bar x_1)+f_2(\bar x_2).\] The infimal convolution is exact at \(x\) if at least one such pair exists. Its common-subgradient certificate set is \[K(x;\bar x_1,\bar x_2):=\partial f_1(\bar x_1)\cap\partial f_2(\bar x_2).\] Under the standard common-affine-minorant regime, exactness yields \[\partial(f_1\square f_2)(x)=K(x;\bar x_1,\bar x_2).\] Exactness does not require the decomposition to be unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact infimal decomposition is a feasible splitting of \(x\) that attains the infimum defining the infimal convolution. Associated with any exact splitting is the intersection of the two component subdifferentials. In the supported convex regime, this intersection equals the subdifferential of the infimal convolution and therefore does not depend on which exact decomposition is selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(f_1\square f_2)(x)=f_1(\bar x_1)+f_2(\bar x_2),\qquad \partial(f_1\square f_2)(x)=\partial f_1(\bar x_1)\cap\partial f_2(\bar x_2).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Exactness is equivalent to \((\bar x_1,\bar x_2)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_1+x_2=x}[f_1(x_1)+f_2(x_2)]\).
special_cases_latex: If one component is differentiable at its exact component, every common subgradient must equal that component gradient.
immediate_consequences_latex: Different exact decompositions produce the same common-subgradient set whenever the exact rule applies.
boundary_notes: Exactness is a pointwise property and need not hold at every point of the domain.
Exactness does not imply that the infimal convolution is globally lower semicontinuous.

children.title: Infimal-Convolution Attainment Boundary
children.top_down_role: Infimal-convolution behavior requiring closure or approximate decompositions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonattained infimal-decomposition boundary
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(h=f_1\square f_2\) be a proper convex infimal convolution on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and fix \(x\in\operatorname{dom}h\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise nonattainment and closure phenomena for finite-dimensional convex infimal convolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varepsilon>0\), define \[D_\varepsilon(x):=\{(x_1,x_2):x_1+x_2=x,\ f_1(x_1)+f_2(x_2)\le h(x)+\varepsilon\}.\] The point \(x\) lies on the infimal-convolution attainment boundary when \[D_\varepsilon(x)\neq\varnothing\ \text{for every }\varepsilon>0,\qquad D_0(x)=\varnothing.\] A sequence \((x_{1,k},x_{2,k})\) is an approximate decomposition if \(x_{1,k}+x_{2,k}=x\) and \[f_1(x_{1,k})+f_2(x_{2,k})\downarrow h(x).\] The closed infimal convolution is the lower-semicontinuous hull \[\overline h:=\operatorname{cl}h,\qquad \operatorname{epi}\overline h=\overline{\operatorname{epi}h}.\] These objects distinguish failure of minimizer attainment from failure of epigraphical closedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an attainment-boundary point, arbitrarily accurate decompositions exist but no exact minimizing decomposition exists. Approximate decomposition sequences approach the infimal value while their components may escape or fail to converge. Separately, the infimal convolution may fail to be lower semicontinuous, in which case its epigraphical closure is recorded by the lower-semicontinuous hull. Nonattainment and nonclosedness are distinct boundary phenomena.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Nonattainment means that the infimum defining \(h(x)\) is finite but is not a minimum.
special_cases_latex: If an approximate decomposition sequence has a convergent subsequence and both functions are lower semicontinuous at its limit components, the boundary point becomes attained.
immediate_consequences_latex: The exact common-subgradient formula cannot be invoked through a pair in \(D_0(x)\) when that set is empty.
boundary_notes: Nonattainment does not by itself imply \(h(x)\ne(\operatorname{cl}h)(x)\).
The record defines the boundary objects but does not assert a general approximate-subgradient equality.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x^*\in X^*\), define \((f^*\square g^*)(x^*)=\inf\{f^*(u^*)+g^*(v^*):u^*+v^*=x^*\}\). The conjugate of the sum satisfies \[(f+g)^*(x^*)=\operatorname{cl}(f^*\square g^*)(x^*).\] Thus closure is required unless an additional qualification guarantees that the infimal convolution is lower semicontinuous. When the infimum is attained and no closure gap occurs, the right-hand side equals the minimum over exact dual decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of a sum is the lower-semicontinuous closure of the infimal convolution of the conjugates; attainment or qualification can make the closure unnecessary.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The functions \(p(u)=e^u\) and \(q(v)=0\) are proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex. For every \(y\in\mathbb R\), \[(p\square q)(y)=\inf_{u\in\mathbb R}\bigl(e^u+q(y-u)\bigr)=\inf_{u\in\mathbb R}e^u=0.\] No finite \(u\) realizes this value. Hence the infimal convolution is finite and closed, while every exact decomposition \(y=u+(y-u)\) has objective value strictly greater than its infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two closed convex functions can have a finite infimal convolution whose defining decomposition infimum is never attained.

children.top_down_role: Subdifferential behavior under elimination through linear mappings.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Infimal image under a linear mapping
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be a surjective linear map and let \(g:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper convex and bounded below on every fiber \(A^{-1}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex elimination through a surjective linear mapping, with an attained fiber at the point of subdifferentiation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The infimal image of \(g\) under \(A\) and its minimizing fiber are \[(Ag)(x):=\inf\{g(y):Ay=x\},\qquad Y(x):=\{y:Ay=x,\ g(y)=(Ag)(x)\}.\] If \(Y(x)\neq\varnothing\), the linear-elimination subgradient set is \[E(x;y):=\{s\in\mathbb{R}^n:A^*s\in\partial g(y)\},\qquad y\in Y(x).\] The calculus rule is \[\partial(Ag)(x)=E(x;y).\] Hence the set is independent of the chosen minimizing fiber point. For the coordinate projection \(A(x,y)=x\), this becomes \[\partial p(x)=\{s:(s,0)\in\partial g(x,y)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear-elimination calculus defines a value function by minimizing a convex function over each affine fiber of a surjective linear map. At an attained fiber, a vector is a subgradient of the value function exactly when its adjoint lift is a subgradient of the original function at a minimizing point. Coordinate projection gives ordinary partial minimization.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For coordinate elimination, \(A^*s=(s,0)\), so \(\partial p(x)=\{s:(s,0)\in\partial g(x,y)\}\).
special_cases_latex: The addition map \(A(y_1,y_2)=y_1+y_2\) produces infimal convolution.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(g\) is differentiable at a minimizing fiber point, injectivity of \(A^*\) gives at most one marginal subgradient.
boundary_notes: If the fiber minimum is not attained, the displayed formula has no minimizing point at which to evaluate \(\partial g\).
Nonsurjective maps require restriction to the range and corresponding relative-space conventions.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the linear-image marginal by \[g(y)=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ Ax=y\},\] using \(+\infty\) when the fiber is empty. Then, for every \(y^*\in Y^*\), its Fenchel conjugate is \[g^*(y^*)=f^*(A^*y^*).\] This identity does not require fiberwise attainment. children.title: Set-Induced Subdifferential Calculus
children.top_down_role: Normal-cone and exposed-face rules obtained through indicator and support representations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Indicator, normal cone, support function, and exposed face
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex-set calculus induced by indicator and support-function representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the indicator and support functions by \[\delta_C(x):=\begin{cases}0,&x\in C,\\+\infty,&x\notin C,\end{cases}\qquad \sigma_C(u):=\sup_{z\in C}\langle u,z\rangle.\] For \(x\in C\), the normal cone is \[N_C(x):=\{u:\langle u,z-x\rangle\le0\ \text{for every }z\in C\}=\partial\delta_C(x).\] For \(u\in\operatorname{dom}\sigma_C\), the exposed face is \[F_C(u):=\{x\in C:\langle u,x\rangle=\sigma_C(u)\}.\] Whenever the supremum is attained, \[F_C(u)=\partial\sigma_C(u),\qquad u\in N_C(x)\Longleftrightarrow x\in F_C(u).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Set-induced subdifferential calculus represents a closed convex set through its indicator and support functions. The indicator subdifferential is the normal cone. A direction exposes the points maximizing its linear functional; this exposed face is the support-function subdifferential when the maximum is attained. Normality and exposed-face membership are reciprocal descriptions of the same pairing.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(u\in N_C(x)\) is equivalent to \(\sigma_C(u)=\langle u,x\rangle\).
special_cases_latex: If \(C\) is compact, \(F_C(u)\neq\varnothing\) for every \(u\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Support functions depend only on \(\overline{\operatorname{co}}C\).
boundary_notes: For unbounded \(C\), \(\sigma_C(u)\) may equal \(+\infty\), and an exposed face may be empty.
The normal cone is empty outside \(C\) under the convex-subdifferential convention.

notation.meaning: face of C exposed by u

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Qualified normal-cone intersection calculus
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty closed convex sets, let \(C:=\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i\), and fix \(x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite intersections of closed convex sets in finite dimensions under a relative-interior qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The unconditional normal-cone inclusion is \[\sum_{i=1}^m N_{C_i}(x)\subseteq N_C(x).\] The family is qualified when \[\bigcap_{i=1}^m\operatorname{ri}C_i\neq\varnothing.\] Under this qualification, the normal-cone intersection rule is exact: \[N_{\cap_{i=1}^m C_i}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m N_{C_i}(x)\] \[=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m u_i:u_i\in N_{C_i}(x)\right\}.\] Equivalently, since \(\delta_C=\sum_i\delta_{C_i}\), this is the qualified convex subdifferential sum rule for indicator functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite intersection of closed convex sets, sums of normals to the individual sets are always normal to the intersection. If the relative interiors of all sets have a common point, every normal to the intersection decomposes as a sum of individual normals. This is exactly the indicator-function subdifferential sum rule.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\partial(\sum_i\delta_{C_i})(x)=\sum_i\partial\delta_{C_i}(x)\) under the same qualification.
special_cases_latex: For affine subspaces with nonempty intersection, the rule gives the sum of their orthogonal normal subspaces.
immediate_consequences_latex: A normal to a qualified intersection admits multiplier-like component normals.
boundary_notes: Without qualification, only the displayed inclusion is guaranteed; equality may fail.
The formula concerns finite intersections, not arbitrary infinite intersections.

notation.meaning: Minkowski sum of the component normal cones

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Product and affine inverse-image normal calculus
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C_i\subset\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) be nonempty closed convex sets. Let \(A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be linear, \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and let \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^m\) be nonempty closed convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex products and affine inverse images under a relative-interior range qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x_i\in C_i\), product normal calculus is \[N_{C_1\times\cdots\times C_k}(x_1,\ldots,x_k)=N_{C_1}(x_1)\times\cdots\times N_{C_k}(x_k).\] Define the affine inverse image \[S:=\{x:Ax+b\in D\}.\] If the range qualification \[(b+\operatorname{range}A)\cap\operatorname{ri}D\neq\varnothing\] holds, then for every \(x\in S\), \[N_S(x)=A^*N_D(Ax+b)=\{A^*v:v\in N_D(Ax+b)\}.\] For the affine equality set \(S=\{x:Ax=b_0\}\), this specializes to \(N_S(x)=\operatorname{range}A^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normal cones factor componentwise over Cartesian products. For an affine inverse image of a convex set, a relative-interior range qualification permits every normal to be obtained by lifting a normal to the target set through the adjoint map. Affine equality constraints reduce this construction to the range of the adjoint.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The inverse-image formula is the indicator composition rule \(\partial(\delta_D\circ(A\cdot+b))(x)=A^*\partial\delta_D(Ax+b)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(D=\{b_0\}\), then \(N_{\{x:Ax+b=b_0\}}(x)=\operatorname{range}A^*\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Normals to separable product constraints can be chosen independently by block.
boundary_notes: Without the inverse-image qualification, the adjoint image is always a natural candidate but equality can fail.
The affine equality set must be nonempty for its normal cone to be evaluated.

notation.meaning: adjoint of the linear mapping A

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\) be a positive integer. For the product set \(C=C_1\times\cdots\times C_m\) and any \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in C\), the normal cone separates componentwise: \[N_C(x)=N_{C_1}(x_1)\times\cdots\times N_{C_m}(x_m).\] Equivalently, \(u=(u_1,\ldots,u_m)\) is normal to \(C\) at \(x\) if and only if \(u_i\in N_{C_i}(x_i)\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). No intersection qualification is required for this product identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite family of nonempty closed convex sets in Hilbert spaces, the normal cone to their Cartesian product is the Cartesian product of the factor normal cones.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support-function and exposed-face operation calculus
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C,D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty closed convex sets, let \(t>0\), and let \(A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be linear.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional support-function calculus; exposed-face identities are asserted when the relevant support suprema are attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The support function is \(\sigma_C(u)=\sup_{x\in C}\langle u,x\rangle\), and its exposed face is \(F_C(u)=\{x\in C:\langle u,x\rangle=\sigma_C(u)\}\). The canonical operation rules are \[\sigma_{tC}=t\sigma_C,\qquad \sigma_{C+D}=\sigma_C+\sigma_D,\qquad \sigma_{A(C)}(v)=\sigma_C(A^*v),\] \[\sigma_{\overline{\operatorname{co}}(C\cup D)}=\max\{\sigma_C,\sigma_D\}.\] When the corresponding maxima are attained, \[F_{C+D}(u)=F_C(u)+F_D(u),\qquad F_{A(C)}(v)=A(F_C(A^*v)),\] and the exposed face of \(\overline{\operatorname{co}}(C\cup D)\) is the convex hull of the faces belonging to sets attaining the larger support value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support functions transform scaling into scaling, Minkowski addition into function addition, linear images into adjoint composition, and closed convex hulls of unions into pointwise maxima. When support values are attained, the corresponding subdifferentials describe exposed faces and inherit parallel operation rules.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The support-function correspondence converts geometric set operations into convex functional operations.
special_cases_latex: For compact \(C\) and \(D\), all exposed faces in the displayed formulas are nonempty for every direction.
immediate_consequences_latex: \(\sigma_C=\sigma_{\overline{\operatorname{co}}C}\), so the support function determines a closed convex set uniquely.
boundary_notes: For unbounded sets, support functions may be extended-valued.
Linear images or Minkowski sums may require closure when interpreted as closed convex sets, although their support functions are unchanged by closure.

notation.meaning: face of C exposed by u

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subdifferential-integral interchange structure
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mu)\) be a measure space and let \(f:\Omega\times\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be measurable in \(\omega\) and proper lower-semicontinuous convex in \(x\) for almost every \(\omega\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional integral convex functionals; this candidate records the interchange object but lacks an inspected authoritative locator for the exact qualification regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the integral functional by \[I(x):=\int_\Omega f(\omega,x)\,d\mu(\omega),\] whenever the extended integral is well defined. For fixed \(x\), define the integrable subgradient-selection set \[\mathcal S(x):=\{s:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^n:s\text{ is measurable and integrable, }s(\omega)\in\partial_x f(\omega,x)\text{ a.e.}\}.\] The interchange set is the Aumann integral \[\int_\Omega\partial_x f(\omega,x)\,d\mu:=\left\{\int_\Omega s(\omega)\,d\mu:s\in\mathcal S(x)\right\}.\] An exact subdifferential-integral interchange regime is one in which \[\partial I(x)=\int_\Omega\partial_x f(\omega,x)\,d\mu.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The calculus object consists of an integral convex functional, measurable integrable selections from the pointwise subdifferentials, and the set of their integrals. Exact interchange means that this selection integral equals the subdifferential of the integral functional. Measurability, integrability, normal-integrand, and qualification conditions are essential to any theorem asserting the equality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial I(x)=\left\{\int_\Omega s(\omega)\,d\mu:s(\omega)\in\partial_xf(\omega,x)\ \text{a.e.}\right\}\] defines an exact interchange regime.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a probability measure, \(I(x)=\mathbb E[f(\omega,x)]\) and the selection integral is an expectation of measurable pointwise subgradients.
special_cases_latex: A finite atomic probability space reduces the construction to a weighted finite subdifferential sum.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every integrable pointwise subgradient selection supplies a candidate aggregate subgradient whenever the interchange equality holds.
boundary_notes: Pointwise convexity alone does not guarantee measurability, integrability, or exact interchange.
No infinite-dimensional Bochner-space or decomposability variant is asserted.
review_flags: No supplied authoritative-source hint was found to support the exact measurable-selection and subdifferential-interchange scope.
A precise normal-integrand theorem and its qualification hypotheses must be sourced before promotion.
knowledge_statements.title: Subdifferential-integral interchange structure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted finite-scenario subdifferential aggregation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), \(i=1,\ldots,N\), be proper convex functions, and let \(p_i\ge0\) with \(\sum_{i=1}^Np_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite deterministic scenario aggregation and sample-average functions in finite-dimensional convex analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The discrete scenario aggregate and its scenario-subgradient aggregation set are \[F(x):=\sum_{i=1}^Np_i f_i(x),\qquad \mathcal A(x):=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^Np_i s_i:s_i\in\partial f_i(x)\right\}.\] If the weighted summands satisfy a finite-sum qualification, for example \[\bigcap_{i:p_i>0}\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f_i)\neq\varnothing,\] then the exact aggregation rule is \[\partial F(x)=\mathcal A(x)=\sum_{i=1}^Np_i\partial f_i(x).\] The sample-average specialization uses \(p_i=1/N\): \[F_N(x)=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^Nf_i(x),\qquad \partial F_N(x)=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\partial f_i(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discrete scenario aggregate is a convex combination of scenario functions. Its aggregation set consists of the same convex combination of one subgradient selected from each scenario. Under the standard relative-interior qualification, this set is exactly the subdifferential of the aggregate. Equal weights give the sample-average rule.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(s\in\partial F(x)\) exactly when \(s=\sum_ip_is_i\) for suitable \(s_i\in\partial f_i(x)\), under the stated qualification.
special_cases_latex: If every \(f_i\) is differentiable at \(x\), then \(\nabla F(x)=\sum_ip_i\nabla f_i(x)\).
Equal weights yield the sample-average function.
immediate_consequences_latex: A scenario with \(p_i=0\) has no effect on the aggregate or its subdifferential.
boundary_notes: For extended-valued functions, the finite-sum qualification cannot generally be omitted.
This finite atomic rule does not by itself establish interchange for a nonatomic expectation.

children.title: Finite-Sum Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Subdifferential organization for finite collections of convex terms.

assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional convex sum rule under a relative-interior qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)\). Under the stated common relative-interior qualification, the convex subdifferential of the finite sum is the Minkowski sum of the individual subdifferentials:
\[\partial F(x)=\partial f_1(x)+\cdots+\partial f_m(x)=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m v_i:v_i\in\partial f_i(x)\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a common relative-interior qualification, the subdifferential of a finite convex sum equals the Minkowski sum of the individual subdifferentials.

children.title: Integral Interchange Regimes
children.top_down_role: Measurability, selection, and qualification interfaces for integral subdifferentiation.

assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mu)\) is a finite measure space and \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\times\Omega\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is a convex normal integrand.
\(F(x)=\int_\Omega f(x,\omega)\,d\mu(\omega)\) is proper and finite on a neighborhood of the evaluation point.
The multifunction \(\omega\mapsto\partial_x f(x,\omega)\) has integrable measurable selections.
review_flags: exact interchange theorem and domination hypotheses require authoritative source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A standard finite-dimensional sufficient regime; sharper normal-integrand variants may weaken local finiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In this regime, every integrable measurable selection \(v(\omega)\in\partial_x f(x,\omega)\) yields \(\int_[0mOmega v\,d\mu\in\partial F(x)\). If local integrable domination and the stated qualification permit separation and measurable selection, the reverse inclusion also holds, giving
\[\partial F(x)=\int_\Omega^{A}\partial_x f(x,\omega)\,d\mu(\omega).\]
The equality is not asserted when measurability, integrable selection, or qualification fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measurability, integrable selections, and a local qualification permit the subdifferential of a convex integral to equal the Aumann integral of pointwise subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.title: Integral Interchange Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equality depends on precise domination, measurability, closure, and selection hypotheses that are only described conditionally, and no authoritative source is cited. The expression containing `\int_[0mOmega` is also malformed. Source verification is required before selecting an exact theorem regime.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact integral–subdifferential interchange regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \((\Omega,\mathcal A,\mu)\) is a complete finite measure space, \(X=\mathbb R^n\), and \(h:\Omega\times X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is a convex normal integrand. Define \(H(x)=\int_\Omega h(\omega,x)\,d\mu(\omega)\) whenever the integral is well defined, and let the integral of a multifunction be understood in the Aumann sense through integrable measurable selections.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Candidate finite-dimensional exact-interchange interface. It records the measurability, selection, integrability, and qualification conditions that an integral subdifferentiation regime must expose; no infinite-dimensional or singular-dual formula is included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\mathcal R(h,\bar x):=\left\{\text{conditions ensuring }H\text{ is proper and }\partial H(\bar x)=\left\{\int_\Omega s(\omega)\,d\mu(\omega):s\in L^1(\mu;X),\ s(\omega)\in\partial h(\omega,\bar x)\ \mu\text{-a.e.}\right\}\right\}.\] An exact integral-interchange regime is a specified collection \(\mathcal R(h,\bar x)\) that additionally guarantees measurable selection and integrability of the pointwise subgradient multifunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact integral-interchange regime for a convex normal integrand is a stated collection of hypotheses under which the integral functional is proper and its subdifferential at the base point equals the Aumann integral of the pointwise subdifferentials. The regime must explicitly guarantee measurability of the pointwise multifunction, existence of integrable selections, and the qualification needed for equality.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[x^*\in\partial H(\bar x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists s\in L^1(\mu;X):\ s(\omega)\in\partial h(\omega,\bar x)\ \mu\text{-a.e.},\quad x^*=\int_\Omega s\,d\mu.\]

immediate_consequences_latex: Whenever the equality is valid, every integrable pointwise subgradient selection supplies a subgradient of \(H\), and every subgradient of \(H\) admits such a selection representation.
boundary_notes: The displayed equality is not asserted without the regime’s qualification and selection hypotheses.
Infinite-dimensional spaces can require weak-star measurable selections and singular dual components not represented by a Bochner integral.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex epsilon-subdifferential
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(X=\mathbb R^n\) with its Euclidean pairing, \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex, \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and \(\varepsilon\ge 0\). For \(x\notin\operatorname{dom}f\), set \(\partial_\varepsilon f(x)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex epsilon-subdifferential defined by a global relaxed supporting inequality. The same inequality can be applied to a nonconvex function finite at the base point, but the structural consequences recorded here use closed convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\partial_\varepsilon f(x):=\left\{s\in X: f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle s,y-x\rangle-\varepsilon\quad\forall y\in X\right\}.\] An element of this set is an \(\varepsilon\)-subgradient of \(f\) at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The epsilon-subdifferential of a proper closed convex function at a point in its domain is the set of all slopes whose affine model lies below the function everywhere after allowing a vertical error of at most epsilon.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\iff \forall y\in X,\quad f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle s,y-x\rangle-\varepsilon.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Because \(f(y)=+\infty\) off its domain, the universal quantifier may equivalently be restricted to \(y\in\operatorname{dom}f\).
\[s\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\iff f^*(s)+f(x)-\langle s,x\rangle\le\varepsilon.\]
special_cases_latex: \(\partial_0f(x)=\partial f(x)\), the exact convex subdifferential.
For a closed convex set \(C\) and \(x\in C\), \(\partial_\varepsilon\iota_C(x)=\{s:\langle s,y-x\rangle\le\varepsilon\ \forall y\in C\}\), the epsilon-normal set.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(0\le\varepsilon\le\varepsilon'\), then \(\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\subseteq\partial_{\varepsilon'}f(x)\).
\[\partial f(x)=\bigcap_{\varepsilon>0}\partial_\varepsilon f(x).\]
Each \(\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\) is closed and convex; for \(\varepsilon>0\), it is nonempty at every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) in the stated finite-dimensional closed-convex setting.
boundary_notes: For \(\varepsilon>0\), the definition is global rather than purely local.
At boundary points of \(\operatorname{dom}f\), the set can be unbounded.
The tolerance is additive in function values and is not a norm bound on the subgradient error.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent representations of an approximate subgradient
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(X=\mathbb R^n\), \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex, \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), \(s\in X\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Define the Fenchel residual \(\delta_f(x,s)=f(x)+f^*(s)-\langle s,x\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional representation dictionary linking relaxed affine support, the Fenchel gap, conjugate symmetry, and the tolerance-indexed graph. It concerns additive epsilon-subgradients, not metric approximations of gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[s\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\bigl[\forall y\in X,\ f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle s,y-x\rangle-\varepsilon\bigr]\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\delta_f(x,s)\le\varepsilon\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\partial_\varepsilon f^*(s).\] These equivalent conditions constitute the canonical primal, conjugate, and graph representations of the approximate subgradient pair \((x,s)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pair is an approximate primal subgradient pair exactly when its globally supporting affine model misses the function by at most epsilon, equivalently when its Fenchel–Young gap is at most epsilon, equivalently when the primal point is an epsilon-subgradient of the conjugate at the dual point.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\delta_f(x,s)=\sup_{y\in X}\{f(x)+\langle s,y-x\rangle-f(y)\}.\]
\[s\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\iff (s,x)\in\operatorname{gra}\partial_\varepsilon f^*.\]
special_cases_latex: At \(\varepsilon=0\), the conditions reduce to Fenchel–Young equality and exact conjugate subgradient reciprocity.
For \(f=\iota_C\), the residual is \(\sigma_C(s)-\langle s,x\rangle\), yielding the epsilon-normal representation.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every approximate subgradient belongs to \(\operatorname{dom}f^*\).
The smallest tolerance certifying a fixed pair \((x,s)\) is exactly \(\delta_f(x,s)\).
For fixed \(x\), \(\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\) is the \(\varepsilon\)-sublevel set of \(s\mapsto f^*(s)-\langle s,x\rangle+f(x)\).
boundary_notes: Closed convexity is used for the symmetric statement involving \(f^{**}=f\).
The residual is generally not a distance from \(s\) to \(\partial f(x)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A vector \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\) belongs to \(\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\) if and only if
\[f(y)\geq f(x)+\langle v,y-x\rangle-\varepsilon\qquad\text{for every }y\in\mathbb{R}^n.\]
Equivalently, \(m_{x,v,\varepsilon}(y)=f(x)+\langle v,y-x\rangle-\varepsilon\) is a global affine minorant of \(f\), with \(f(x)-m_{x,v,\varepsilon}(x)=\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An epsilon-subgradient defines a global affine lower model whose shortfall from the function at the base point is at most epsilon.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fenchel--Young inequality gives \(G_f(x,v)=f(x)+f^*(v)-\langle v,x\rangle\geq0\). Moreover,
\[v\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad G_f(x,v)\leq\varepsilon.\]
Thus the computable primal-dual pair \((x,v)\), together with finite values of \(f(x)\) and \(f^*(v)\), certifies approximate subgradient membership precisely when its Fenchel--Young gap does not exceed \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual pair certifies epsilon-subgradient membership exactly when its nonnegative Fenchel-Young gap is at most epsilon.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Approximate Fenchel–Young certificate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(X=\mathbb R^n\), \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex, \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and \(s\in\operatorname{dom}f^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional additive certificate for approximate subgradient membership. The certificate is the numerical Fenchel–Young residual attached to one primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\delta_f(x,s):=f(x)+f^*(s)-\langle s,x\rangle\in[0,+\infty].\] The pair \((x,s)\) is said to possess an \(\varepsilon\)-Fenchel certificate when \(\delta_f(x,s)\le\varepsilon\); equivalently, \(s\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\). The exact certificate value is \(\varepsilon_{\min}(x,s):=\delta_f(x,s)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The approximate Fenchel certificate of a primal-dual pair is its nonnegative Fenchel–Young residual. A tolerance epsilon certifies approximate subgradient membership precisely when it dominates that residual, and the residual itself is the least admissible tolerance.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\delta_f(x,s)\le\varepsilon\iff f^*(s)\le\langle s,x\rangle-f(x)+\varepsilon.\]
\[\delta_f(x,s)\le\varepsilon\iff x\in\partial_\varepsilon f^*(s).\]
special_cases_latex: The certificate is exact when \(\delta_f(x,s)=0\), in which case \(s\in\partial f(x)\).
For \(s=0\), \(\delta_f(x,0)=f(x)-\inf f\); hence \(0\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\) exactly when \(x\) is epsilon-optimal.
immediate_consequences_latex: Increasing the allowed tolerance preserves validity of a certificate.
The certificate supplies a scalar measure of violation of Fenchel–Young equality without requiring an exact subgradient at \(x\).
boundary_notes: The residual can be infinite when \(s\notin\operatorname{dom}f^*\).
A small Fenchel residual does not by itself give a norm estimate to an exact subgradient without additional regularity.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The enlarged graph at tolerance \(\varepsilon\) is
\[\operatorname{gra}\partial_\varepsilon f=\{(x,v)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n:G_f(x,v)\leq\varepsilon\}.\]
It contains \(\operatorname{gra}\partial f\), and for \(0\leq\varepsilon_1\leq\varepsilon_2\) one has \(\operatorname{gra}\partial_{\varepsilon_1}f\subseteq\operatorname{gra}\partial_{\varepsilon_2}f\). Hence a single gap function organizes all inexact primal-dual pairs by accuracy level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The epsilon-subdifferential graph is the epsilon-sublevel set of the Fenchel-Young gap, producing nested enlargements of the exact graph.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tolerance-enlarged subdifferential graph
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(X=\mathbb R^n\), \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Define \(\delta_f(x,s)=f(x)+f^*(s)-\langle s,x\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel-residual enlargement of the graph of a convex subdifferential. This is the graph of the epsilon-subdifferential and is distinguished from other enlargements defined only through monotonicity inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[G_\varepsilon(f):=\operatorname{gra}\partial_\varepsilon f:=\left\{(x,s)\in X\times X:\ x\in\operatorname{dom}f,\ \delta_f(x,s)\le\varepsilon\right\}.\] The full tolerance graph is \(\mathcal G(f):=\{(\varepsilon,x,s)\in\mathbb R_+\times X\times X:(x,s)\in G_\varepsilon(f)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The epsilon-enlarged subdifferential graph consists of all primal-dual pairs whose Fenchel–Young residual is at most epsilon. Collecting these slices over all nonnegative tolerances produces the full tolerance graph.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For fixed \(x\), the vertical section satisfies \(G_\varepsilon(f)_x=\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\).
For fixed \(x\), if \(g_x(y)=f(x+y)-f(x)\), then \(\{(s,\varepsilon):(\varepsilon,x,s)\in\mathcal G(f)\}=\operatorname{epi}g_x^*\).
special_cases_latex: \(G_0(f)=\operatorname{gra}\partial f\).
If \(f\) is affine, every nonempty slice \(G_\varepsilon(f)_x\) is the singleton containing its slope.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(0\le\varepsilon\le\varepsilon'\), then \(G_\varepsilon(f)\subseteq G_{\varepsilon'}(f)\).
The full graph \(\mathcal G(f)\) is closed, and each fixed-base-point set \(\{(\varepsilon,s):s\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\}\) is convex.
Swapping primal and dual coordinates maps \(G_\varepsilon(f)\) onto \(G_\varepsilon(f^*)\).
boundary_notes: This graph enlargement is controlled by a function-value residual, not by a Euclidean tube around \(\operatorname{gra}\partial f\).
Different monotone-operator enlargement conventions need not coincide with this definition for a general operator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epsilon-directional derivative
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(X=\mathbb R^n\), \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex, \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), \(d\in X\), and \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional additive approximate directional object defined as the support function of the epsilon-subdifferential. The positive-tolerance assumption is essential for the unclosed infimum formula stated here.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[f'_\varepsilon(x;d):=\sigma_{\partial_\varepsilon f(x)}(d)=\sup_{s\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)}\langle s,d\rangle=\inf_{t>0}\frac{f(x+td)-f(x)+\varepsilon}{t}.\] This positively homogeneous, closed convex function of \(d\) is the epsilon-directional derivative of \(f\) at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The epsilon-directional derivative at a base point is the support function of the epsilon-subdifferential. For positive epsilon, it is equivalently the infimum over positive step lengths of the forward difference quotient with epsilon added to the numerator.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\partial_\varepsilon f(x)=\{s\in X:\langle s,d\rangle\le f'_\varepsilon(x;d)\ \forall d\in X\}.\]
\[f'_\varepsilon(x;d)=\sup\{\langle s,d\rangle:f^*(s)+f(x)-\langle s,x\rangle\le\varepsilon\}.\]
special_cases_latex: When \(d=0\), \(f'_\varepsilon(x;0)=0\) whenever \(\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\neq\varnothing\).

At \(\varepsilon=0\), the support function of \(\partial f(x)\) agrees with the closed hull of the ordinary directional derivative; equality with the raw directional derivative can fail at boundary points.
immediate_consequences_latex: The map \(d\mapsto f'_\varepsilon(x;d)\) determines the closed convex set \(\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\) uniquely.
If \(0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon'\), then \(f'_\varepsilon(x;d)\le f'_{\varepsilon'}(x;d)\) for every \(d\).
boundary_notes: The quantity may be \(+\infty\) in directions incompatible with the effective domain.
It is not obtained by merely adding epsilon to the ordinary directional derivative; the term is divided by the step length before minimization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epsilon-Subgradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the tolerance-dependent relaxation of the convex subgradient inequality for a convex function finite at the base point and a strictly positive tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f be convex and finite at x, and let \varepsilon>0. A vector x^* is an \varepsilon-subgradient of f at x if f(z)\geq f(x)-\varepsilon+\langle x^*,z-x\rangle for every z. The set of all such vectors is denoted by \partial_\varepsilon f(x).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex function finite at x and a positive tolerance epsilon, an epsilon-subgradient is a vector whose affine support inequality is allowed an error of epsilon and remains valid for every z. The set of all epsilon-subgradients is the epsilon-subdifferential.

Define

Then the approximate directional derivative is the support function of the approximate subdifferential:
\[f'_\varepsilon(x;d)=\sigma_{\partial_\varepsilon f(x)}(d)=\sup_{v\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)}\langle v,d\rangle.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support–directional correspondence at positive tolerance
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(X=\mathbb R^n\), \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex, \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and \(\varepsilon>0\). Set \(q_\varepsilon(x,d;t)=[f(x+td)-f(x)+\varepsilon]/t\) for \(t>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence between the support geometry of the epsilon-subdifferential and a tolerance-shifted directional quotient. It is a set/function dictionary rather than a new subdifferential notion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\sigma_{\partial_\varepsilon f(x)}(d)=\inf_{t>0}q_\varepsilon(x,d;t)\quad\forall d\in X,\qquad \partial_\varepsilon f(x)=\bigcap_{d\in X}\left\{s:\langle s,d\rangle\le\inf_{t>0}q_\varepsilon(x,d;t)\right\}.\] This pair of mutually determining formulas is the approximate support–directional correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At positive tolerance, the support value of the approximate subdifferential in any direction equals the smallest epsilon-shifted forward quotient along that direction. Conversely, intersecting all half-spaces determined by these directional values recovers the approximate subdifferential.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For every \(d\), \(\langle s,d\rangle\le f'_\varepsilon(x;d)\) for all directions if and only if \(s\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\).
The directional function \(f'_\varepsilon(x;\cdot)\) is the support function of a unique nonempty closed convex set, namely \(\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\).
special_cases_latex: For \(f=\iota_C\), the formula describes the support function of the epsilon-normal set to \(C\).
For an affine \(f(y)=\langle a,y\rangle+b\), both sides equal \(\langle a,d\rangle\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Directional quotient information in every direction reconstructs all epsilon-subgradients.
Any candidate \(s\) is excluded from \(\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\) as soon as one direction satisfies \(\langle s,d\rangle>f'_\varepsilon(x;d)\).
boundary_notes: The positive-tolerance formula must not be transferred unchanged to \(\varepsilon=0\) at an effective-domain boundary.
Knowledge in only finitely many directions generally yields an outer approximation rather than equality.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Tolerance levels produce nested closed convex sets:
\[0\leq\varepsilon_1\leq\varepsilon_2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\partial_{\varepsilon_1}f(x)\subseteq\partial_{\varepsilon_2}f(x).\]
Their zero-tolerance limit is exact:
\[\bigcap_{\varepsilon>0}\partial_\varepsilon f(x)=\partial_0 f(x)=\partial f(x).\]
Equivalently, for fixed \((x,v)\), the smallest admissible tolerance is the Fenchel--Young gap \(f(x)+f^*(v)-\langle v,x\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate subdifferentials expand monotonically with tolerance, shrink to the exact subdifferential at zero, and assign each pair a minimal gap tolerance.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(X=\mathbb R^n\), \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\). Define \(S_x(\varepsilon)=\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\) for \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry of the fixed-base-point multifunction indexed by additive accuracy. It describes nestedness, convexity in the joint tolerance-dual variables, and the exact zero-tolerance limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[S_x(\varepsilon):=\{s\in X:f^*(s)+f(x)-\langle s,x\rangle\le\varepsilon\},\qquad \operatorname{gra}S_x=\{(\varepsilon,s):\varepsilon\ge0,\ s\in S_x(\varepsilon)\}.\] The tolerance-parameter geometry is the nested sublevel-set family \(\{S_x(\varepsilon)\}_{\varepsilon\ge0}\) together with its closed convex joint graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed base point, the approximate subdifferentials form the sublevel sets of the tilted conjugate. These sets expand monotonically with tolerance, their graph in tolerance-dual space is closed and convex, and their decreasing limit at zero is the exact subdifferential.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(g_x(y)=f(x+y)-f(x)\), then \(\operatorname{gra}S_x=\{(\varepsilon,s):(s,\varepsilon)\in\operatorname{epi}g_x^*\}\).
For \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), \(\alpha S_x(\varepsilon)+(1-\alpha)S_x(\varepsilon')\subseteq S_x(\alpha\varepsilon+(1-\alpha)\varepsilon')\).
special_cases_latex: If \(f\) is one-coercive, then \(S_x(\varepsilon)\subset\operatorname{int}S_x(\varepsilon')\) whenever \(0\le\varepsilon<\varepsilon'\).
For an affine function, every tolerance slice is the same singleton.
immediate_consequences_latex: The least tolerance at which a dual point \(s\) enters the family is \(f(x)+f^*(s)-\langle s,x\rangle\).
No subgradient is lost as tolerance increases, and the exact subdifferential is recovered by decreasing positive tolerances to zero.
boundary_notes: Strict expansion need not hold without additional hypotheses; affine functions are a basic exception.
The union over finite tolerances equals \(\operatorname{dom}f^*\), but it need not be closed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tolerance-budget subdifferential calculus
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: All spaces are finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces. The input functions are proper closed convex functions, the constructed function is proper, \(x\) lies in its effective domain, and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of the approximate-calculus paradigm: tolerances are distributed among constituent functions, and exact reverse inclusions require the qualification or attainment condition attached to the functional operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An approximate subdifferential calculus rule for an operation \(\Phi(f_1,\ldots,f_m)\) is an identity or universally valid inclusion of the form \[\partial_\varepsilon\Phi(f_1,\ldots,f_m)(x)=\bigcup_{\theta\in\Theta_\varepsilon(x)}\mathcal C_\theta\bigl(\partial_{\varepsilon_1}f_1(\cdot),\ldots,\partial_{\varepsilon_m}f_m(\cdot)\bigr),\] where \(\theta\) contains nonnegative error allocations, their total prescribed cost is at most \(\varepsilon\), and \(\mathcal C_\theta\) is the dual operation induced by \(\Phi\). Without the relevant qualification, the right-hand side is interpreted only in the source-supported inclusion direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate subdifferential calculus is the family of rules that computes or bounds the epsilon-subdifferential of a convex functional construction by distributing a total nonnegative error budget among the input functions and combining their approximate subgradients through the dual operation. Equality is part of a rule only when its stated qualification or attainment condition holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sum_i\varepsilon_i\le\varepsilon,\quad s_i\in\partial_{\varepsilon_i}f_i(\cdot)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathcal C(s_1,\ldots,s_m)\in\partial_\varepsilon\Phi(f_1,\ldots,f_m)(x),\] with converse representation only under the operation-specific qualification.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The budget condition may frequently be written with equality because \(\partial_\eta f(x)\) is increasing in \(\eta\).
Through \(s\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\iff f^*(s)+f(x)-\langle s,x\rangle\le\varepsilon\), each calculus rule is equivalently a decomposition of a Fenchel residual across the constituent functions.
special_cases_latex: For sums, the dual operation is Minkowski addition.
For affine precomposition, the dual operation is the adjoint linear map.
For marginal functions, the rule imposes a zero dual component in the eliminated variable.
immediate_consequences_latex: Setting \(\varepsilon=0\) recovers the corresponding exact convex subdifferential rule whenever the same qualification applies.
The framework records separately approximation error and qualification failure; the former does not remove the need for the latter.
boundary_notes: Different functional operations have different admissible parameter sets \(\Theta_\varepsilon(x)\).
A universal equality without qualification is not part of this definition.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sum and affine-precomposition epsilon-rules
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f_i:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex functions. Let \(A(x)=A_0x+y_0\) be affine, \(x\) belong to the relevant domains, and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional algebraic family containing the tolerance-budget rule for finite sums and the adjoint rule for affine precomposition. Equalities carry explicit relative-interior qualifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The approximate algebraic rule family is defined by \[\partial_\varepsilon\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\Bigr)(x)=\bigcup_{\substack{\varepsilon_i\ge0\\\sum_i\varepsilon_i\le\varepsilon}}\sum_{i=1}^m\partial_{\varepsilon_i}f_i(x),\qquad \partial_\varepsilon(g\circ A)(x)=A_0^*\partial_\varepsilon g(Ax),\] whenever, respectively, \(\bigcap_i\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f_i)\ne\varnothing\) and \(A(\mathbb R^n)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The approximate algebraic family consists of the finite-sum rule, which distributes epsilon among summands and adds their approximate subgradients, and the affine-precomposition rule, which pulls approximate subgradients back by the adjoint of the linear part. Under the displayed relative-interior qualifications these formulas are equalities.
equivalent_formulations_latex: In the sum rule, \(\sum_i\varepsilon_i\le\varepsilon\) can be replaced by \(\sum_i\varepsilon_i=\varepsilon\).
Without the sum qualification, \(\bigcup_{\sum_i\varepsilon_i\le\varepsilon}\sum_i\partial_{\varepsilon_i}f_i(x)\subseteq\partial_\varepsilon(\sum_i f_i)(x)\).
Without the affine qualification, \(A_0^*\partial_\varepsilon g(Ax)\subseteq\partial_\varepsilon(g\circ A)(x)\).
special_cases_latex: At \(\varepsilon=0\), these formulas reduce to the ordinary convex sum and affine-chain rules.
If \(A_0\) is the identity and \(y_0=0\), the affine rule is tautological.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every allocation of the tolerance budget produces a valid approximate subgradient of the sum.
The affine rule introduces no new tolerance beyond that already assigned to \(g\).
boundary_notes: The reverse inclusions may fail when the corresponding conjugate minimization is not attained.
The affine rule uses the adjoint of the linear part \(A_0\), not the affine map itself.

notation.meaning: adjoint of the linear part of the affine map

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\). Under the relative-interior qualification, every approximate subgradient admits a componentwise decomposition with a conserved error budget: \[\partial_\varepsilon F(x)=\bigcup_{\substack{\varepsilon_i\geq0\\\sum_{i=1}^m\varepsilon_i=\varepsilon}}\left(\partial_{\varepsilon_1}f_1(x)+\cdots+\partial_{\varepsilon_m}f_m(x)\right).\] Thus \(v\in\partial_\varepsilon F(x)\) exactly when \(v=\sum_i v_i\), where \(v_i\in\partial_{\varepsilon_i}f_i(x)\) for an admissible allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under qualification, an epsilon-subgradient of a finite sum decomposes into approximate component subgradients whose nonnegative error budgets total epsilon.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(g(x)=f(Ax+b)\). Under the stated range-relative-interior qualification, the approximate affine chain rule is
\[\partial_\varepsilon g(x)=A^*\partial_\varepsilon f(Ax+b)=\{A^*v:v\in\partial_\varepsilon f(Ax+b)\}.\]
Without this qualification, the inclusion \(A^*\partial_\varepsilon f(Ax+b)\subseteq\partial_\varepsilon g(x)\) remains immediate, while equality or attainment of a representing \(v\) may fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a range-relative-interior qualification, epsilon-subgradients of an affine composite are precisely adjoint images of epsilon-subgradients of the outer function.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-maximum and increasing-composition epsilon-rules
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f_j:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be convex, \(f=\max_{1\le j\le p}f_j\), \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Separately, let \(u:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be convex and \(g:\mathbb R\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper convex and increasing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional extremum and scalar increasing-composition structures. The maximum formula includes approximate activity costs; the composition formula includes both an inner tolerance and an outer tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the maximum, define \(e_j(x)=f(x)-f_j(x)\ge0\). Then \(s\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\) exactly when there exist positive \(\alpha_j\) summing to one, \(\eta_j\ge0\), and \(s_j\in\partial_{\eta_j}f_j(x)\) such that \[s=\sum_j\alpha_js_j,\qquad \sum_j\alpha_j(\eta_j+e_j(x))\le\varepsilon.\] For increasing composition, under \(u(\mathbb R^n)\cap\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}g)\ne\varnothing\), \[s\in\partial_\varepsilon(g\circ u)(x)\iff\exists\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2=\varepsilon,\ \alpha\ge0:\ s\in\partial_{\varepsilon_1}(\alpha u)(x),\ \alpha\in\partial_{\varepsilon_2}g(u(x)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The approximate extremum-composition family represents an epsilon-subgradient of a finite maximum as a convex combination of approximate subgradients whose weighted approximation and inactivity costs fit within epsilon. For an increasing convex outer function, it splits epsilon between an approximate subgradient of a scaled inner function and an approximate scalar subgradient of the outer function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sum_j\alpha_j(\eta_j+f(x)-f_j(x))\le\varepsilon,\quad s=\sum_j\alpha_js_j,\quad s_j\in\partial_{\eta_j}f_j(x),\] together with the displayed two-budget composition characterization.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For the maximum, zero-weight terms can be omitted; an equivalent formulation uses nonnegative \(\varepsilon_j\) with \(s_j\in\partial_{\varepsilon_j/\alpha_j}f_j(x)\).
The epsilon-active set \(J_\varepsilon(x)=\{j:f_j(x)\ge f(x)-\varepsilon\}\) satisfies \(\bigcup_{j\in J_\varepsilon(x)}\partial f_j(x)\subseteq\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\).
special_cases_latex: At \(\varepsilon=0\), only active functions and exact subgradients can receive positive weight.
If \(g(t)=t\), the composition formula reduces to the inner epsilon-subdifferential.
immediate_consequences_latex: Inactivity of a maximum component consumes part of the global tolerance.
The multiplier \(\alpha\) in the composition rule is an approximate subgradient of the scalar outer function.
boundary_notes: The stated maximum equivalence assumes the component functions are finite-valued.
The union over epsilon-active exact subgradients is generally only an inclusion, not the full epsilon-subdifferential.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Marginal and infimal-convolution epsilon-rules
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: All spaces are finite-dimensional. Let \(g:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex and define \(v(x)=\inf_z g(x,z)\). Let \(f_1,f_2:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex and \((f_1\square f_2)(x)=\inf_{y_1+y_2=x}[f_1(y_1)+f_2(y_2)]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact approximate-subdifferential formulas at points where the defining infimum is attained. Relative-interior hypotheses are stated as sufficient attainment qualifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\bar z\) attains \(v(x)=g(x,\bar z)\), then \[\partial_\varepsilon v(x)=\{s\in\mathbb R^n:(s,0)\in\partial_\varepsilon g(x,\bar z)\}.\] If \(x=\bar y_1+\bar y_2\) attains \((f_1\square f_2)(x)=f_1(\bar y_1)+f_2(\bar y_2)\), then \[\partial_\varepsilon(f_1\square f_2)(x)=\bigcup_{\substack{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2\ge0\\\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2\le\varepsilon}}\left(\partial_{\varepsilon_1}f_1(\bar y_1)\cap\partial_{\varepsilon_2}f_2(\bar y_2)\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an attained convex marginal, an epsilon-subgradient of the value function is exactly a joint epsilon-subgradient with zero component in the eliminated variable. For an attained infimal convolution, it is exactly a common approximate subgradient of the two terms at an optimal decomposition, with the two tolerances fitting within the global budget.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A sufficient qualification for the marginal minimizer is the existence of \(s_0\) with \((s_0,0)\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g^*)\).
A sufficient exactness qualification for infimal convolution is \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f_1^*)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f_2^*)\ne\varnothing\).
special_cases_latex: At \(\varepsilon=0\), the infimal-convolution formula becomes \(\partial(f_1\square f_2)(x)=\partial f_1(\bar y_1)\cap\partial f_2(\bar y_2)\).
A linear image value function is covered by replacing the zero-component condition with \(A^*s\in\partial_\varepsilon g(\bar y)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The marginal rule does not depend on which attaining minimizer is chosen after applying the indicated zero-dual-component test.
The infimal-convolution rule uses intersection, contrasting with the Minkowski addition appearing in the sum rule.
boundary_notes: Attainment at the base point is essential to the displayed equalities.
If the infimum is not attained, closure or limiting constructions can be necessary.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tolerance-and-base-point subdifferential multifunction
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(X=\mathbb R^n\) and \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex. The parameter space is \(\mathbb R_+\times X\), and the value space is \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional multifunction retaining both tolerance and base point as variables. It provides the graph used to formulate outer continuity, local boundedness, and positive-tolerance regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\mathsf F_f:\mathbb R_+\times X\rightrightarrows X,\qquad \mathsf F_f(\varepsilon,x):=\partial_\varepsilon f(x)=\{s:f(x)+f^*(s)-\langle s,x\rangle\le\varepsilon\},\] with \(\mathsf F_f(\varepsilon,x)=\varnothing\) when \(x\notin\operatorname{dom}f\). Its graph is \[\operatorname{gra}\mathsf F_f=\{(\varepsilon,x,s):\varepsilon\ge0,\ x\in\operatorname{dom}f,\ f(x)+f^*(s)-\langle s,x\rangle\le\varepsilon\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The approximate subdifferential multifunction maps a tolerance and a base point to the set of all epsilon-subgradients at that point. Its graph is the set of tolerance-primal-dual triples whose Fenchel–Young residual does not exceed the tolerance.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\mathsf F_f(\varepsilon,x)=\{s:f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle s,y-x\rangle-\varepsilon\ \forall y\in X\}.\]
The inverse relation satisfies \(s\in\mathsf F_f(\varepsilon,x)\iff x\in\mathsf F_{f^*}(\varepsilon,s)\).
special_cases_latex: The zero-tolerance section is the exact subdifferential mapping: \(\mathsf F_f(0,x)=\partial f(x)\).
For every \(\varepsilon>0\), the domain of \(x\mapsto\mathsf F_f(\varepsilon,x)\) equals \(\operatorname{dom}f\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The multifunction has a closed graph: if \((\varepsilon_k,x_k,s_k)\to(\varepsilon,x,s)\) and \(s_k\in\mathsf F_f(\varepsilon_k,x_k)\), then \(s\in\mathsf F_f(\varepsilon,x)\).
It is locally bounded in the subgradient coordinate over compact subsets of \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\) when tolerance is locally bounded.
boundary_notes: At \(\varepsilon=0\), inner semicontinuity can fail.
Values can be unbounded at boundary points of the effective domain.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed-graph and positive-tolerance stability regimes
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(X=\mathbb R^n\), \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(\mathsf F_f(\varepsilon,x)=\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\). Hausdorff distance between nonempty compact sets is denoted by \(d_H\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions of two source-supported stability interfaces: sequential outer stability for general closed convex functions and quantitative Hausdorff stability for finite-valued globally Lipschitz convex functions at strictly positive tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The closed-graph stability regime is \[\varepsilon_k\to\varepsilon,\quad x_k\to x,\quad s_k\to s,\quad s_k\in\partial_{\varepsilon_k}f(x_k)\ \Longrightarrow\ s\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x).\] The global positive-tolerance Lipschitz regime holds when \(f\) is convex and Lipschitz on \(X\): there exists \(K>0\) such that \[d_H(\partial_\varepsilon f(x),\partial_{\varepsilon'}f(x'))\le\frac{K}{\min\{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'\}}\bigl(\|x-x'\|+|\varepsilon-\varepsilon'|\bigr)\] for all \(x,x'\in X\) and \(\varepsilon,\varepsilon'>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: General closed convex functions possess sequential outer stability of the tolerance-indexed subdifferential graph. If the function is finite-valued and globally Lipschitz, positive-tolerance values additionally vary Lipschitz-continuously in Hausdorff distance, with sensitivity proportional to the reciprocal of the smaller tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{gra}\mathsf F_f\text{ is closed};\qquad d_H(\mathsf F_f(\varepsilon,x),\mathsf F_f(\varepsilon',x'))\le\frac K{\min\{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'\}}(\|x-x'\|+|\varepsilon-\varepsilon'|)\] in the global Lipschitz regime.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Closed-graph stability is the sequential form of outer semicontinuity in this finite-dimensional setting.
At fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), the quantitative regime gives \(d_H(\partial_\varepsilon f(x),\partial_\varepsilon f(x'))\le(K/\varepsilon)\|x-x'\|\).
special_cases_latex: On compact subsets of \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\), local versions hold with constants depending on the subset.
For finite-valued convex \(f\), fixed positive-tolerance slices are locally Hausdorff-Lipschitz in the base point.
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive tolerance regularizes the base-point dependence compared with the exact subdifferential.
The stability constant deteriorates as tolerance approaches zero.
boundary_notes: The Hausdorff estimate requires positive tolerances and bounded values; it is not an assertion at \(\varepsilon=0\).
For unbounded subdifferential values, truncated-set distances are needed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linearization-error transport of subgradients
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(X=\mathbb R^n\), \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex, \(x,x'\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and \(s'\in\partial f(x')\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact transport certificate from an exact subgradient at one base point to an approximate subgradient at another. An additional one-sided rule is included for transporting an already approximate subgradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the linearization error at \(x\) of the exact supporting plane generated by \((x',s')\) by \[e_f(x;x',s'):=f(x)-f(x')-\langle s',x-x'\rangle\ge0.\] The transported tolerance of \(s'\) from \(x'\) to \(x\) is this error, and \[s'\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\iff e_f(x;x',s')\le\varepsilon.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The transport error is the gap at the target point between the function and the exact affine support generated at the source point. An exact subgradient at the source is an epsilon-subgradient at the target exactly when this error is at most epsilon; the error is therefore the least transport tolerance.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[s'\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\iff f(x')\ge f(x)+\langle s',x'-x\rangle-\varepsilon.\]
Because \(s'\in\partial f(x')\), \(f^*(s')=\langle s',x'\rangle-f(x')\), so the transport error equals the Fenchel residual at \((x,s')\).
special_cases_latex: If \(x=x'\), then \(e_f(x;x',s')=0\) and exact membership is recovered.
If \(s'\in\partial_\eta f(x')\), the sufficient transport condition becomes \(e_f(x;x',s')+\eta\le\varepsilon\), where the same algebraic expression defines \(e_f\).
immediate_consequences_latex: An exact subgradient computed elsewhere can be certified at the target point using only the two function values, the source slope, and the displacement.
No tolerance smaller than the linearization error can contain the transported exact subgradient.
boundary_notes: The biconditional uses exact source membership \(s'\in\partial f(x')\).
For an approximate source subgradient, the stated accumulated-error condition is sufficient but need not be necessary.

children.title: Brøndsted–Rockafellar Approximation Principle
children.top_down_role: Approximation of inexact subgradients by nearby exact subgradients and its graph consequences.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Brøndsted–Rockafellar approximation property
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(X=\mathbb R^n\) with its Euclidean norm, \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex, \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and \(s\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The slot is definition-typed, so the named principle is recorded as the quantified approximation property it asserts. The statement covers finite-dimensional Euclidean convex functions and exact subgradients at nearby points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Brøndsted–Rockafellar approximation property for \(f\) is the assertion that, for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), \(\varepsilon\ge0\), \(s\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\), and \(\eta>0\), there exist \(x_\eta\in X\) and \(s_\eta\in\partial f(x_\eta)\) such that \[\|x_\eta-x\|\le\eta,\qquad \|s_\eta-s\|\le\frac{\varepsilon}{\eta}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Brøndsted–Rockafellar approximation property says that every epsilon-subgradient can be approximated by an exact subgradient at a nearby point. For any chosen spatial radius eta, the point displacement is at most eta and the subgradient displacement is at most epsilon divided by eta.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\subseteq\bigcap_{\eta>0}\bigcup_{\|y-x\|\le\eta}\left(\partial f(y)+B(0,\varepsilon/\eta)\right).\]
Choosing \(\eta=\sqrt\varepsilon\) for \(\varepsilon>0\) yields simultaneous primal and dual deviations bounded by \(\sqrt\varepsilon\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\varepsilon=0\), one may take \(x_\eta=x\) and \(s_\eta=s\).
With \(\eta=\sqrt\varepsilon\), \(s\) lies within \(\sqrt\varepsilon\) of an exact subgradient at a point within \(\sqrt\varepsilon\) of \(x\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every epsilon-subgradient belongs to the closure of the range of the exact subdifferential.
The approximation exposes a reciprocal tradeoff: demanding a smaller base-point displacement permits a larger guaranteed dual displacement.
boundary_notes: The nearby exact subgradient generally need not occur at the original base point.
The estimate does not assert simultaneous errors smaller than the product constraint suggested by \(\eta(\varepsilon/\eta)=\varepsilon\).
The source states this as a named theorem; this definition slot records its quantified property without changing the immutable content kind.

\[
\|\bar x-x\|\leq\lambda,
